documentation: Rules drive LinkedIn Easy Apply auto-fill and Greenhouse checkbox groups. Rules live in this directory (data/form_fill_rules/) as multiple JSON files; every *.json file is loaded in case-insensitive filename order and merged. List keys (screening_yes_no, text_inputs, textareas, selects, checkbox_groups) are concatenated in that order; scalar keys (schema_version, documentation) come from the first file that defines them. Within each list, the FIRST matching rule wins — so files that split one category use numeric prefixes (e.g. screening_10_*.json before screening_20_*.json) to control precedence. Labels are normalized: lowercased and runs of whitespace collapsed to a single space. Matching: all_substrings = every string must appear as a substring; any_substrings = at least one; all_of_any = list of groups — from each group at least one substring must appear; not_substrings = none of these may appear; starts_with = label must start with this text (after normalization); regex = Python regex (default case-insensitive). Results: screening_yes_no uses answer 'Yes' or 'No' for Yes/No radio groups (including LinkedIn ``data-test-form-builder-radio-button-form-component`` fieldsets — legend text is matched, then the option with that label is clicked). Text/select results use type literal, literal_fallbacks, literal_from_apply_source (same ``when`` map as checkbox_groups for free-text fields), name_part, resume_key_list, cover_letter_full, cover_letter_truncated. checkbox_groups: match is the fieldset legend; choose_label is the visible option label. For **How did you hear** when the answer depends on apply channel, use choose_label_from_apply_source on checkbox fieldsets or literal_from_apply_source on text inputs; apply_source is greenhouse for ``--site greenhouse`` and linkedin for LinkedIn Easy Apply. Example: regex "location\\[" matches Workday-style Location[...] labels.
